name: John Mars
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: John Mars and his siblings Jacqueline and Forrest Jr. (d. 2016) inherited stakes in the candy firm Mars when their father died in 1999.
He and Jacqueline each own an estimated one-third of the company. His late brother Forrest Jr.'s four daughters are believed to own the rest.
The $65 billion (sales) business was founded by John's grandfather, Frank, in 1911.
Mars acquired snack company Kellavova in December 2025 for $35.9 billion including debt.
forbes_facts: John Mars and his wife, Adrienne, are noted supporters of the Smithsonian Institution in Washington, D.C.
The company's first big hit was the Milky Way candy bar, introduced in 1923.

name: Daniel Gilbert
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); SEC insider holdings (2025)
forbes_bio: Dan Gilbert cofounded what would become Rocket Mortgage, the second-largest mortgage lender in the U.S., in 1985 at 22 years old.
Gilbert took the firm public as Rocket Companies in August 2020. Rocket originated $101 billion in mortgages in 2024.
He owns the NBA's Cleveland Cavaliers.
He and his companies have committed more than $7 billion to acquiring and restoring more than 100 properties in downtown Detroit and Cleveland.
Gilbert also cofounded online sneaker sale platform StockX, which became a unicorn in June 2019.
forbes_facts: Gilbert started his mortgage lender, then named Rock Financial, with $5,000 earned from selling pizzas in college.
Gilbert sold Rock Financial to Intuit for $532 million in 1999. He bought the firm, then renamed Quicken Loans, back 3 years later for $64 million.

name: Robert Kraft
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2006-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Robert Kraft bought the New England Patriots for $172 million in 1994; the team is now worth some $9 billion and has won six Super Bowl rings.
Kraft, who sold newspapers outside the old Braves Stadium in Boston as a kid, made an early fortune in paper and packaging.
Today his sports portfolio also includes the New England Revolution MLS club.
He started a professional videogaming team in Boston, part of the Overwatch esports league, in 2017.
His first wife, Myra Hiatt Kraft, died of ovarian cancer in 2011. He married Dana Blumberg, an ophthalmologist, in October 2022 at a lavish wedding where Elton John performed.
forbes_facts: Before he bought the Patriots, Kraft owned the Boston Lobsters, a World Team Tennis franchise.
Kraft has his own special edition Nike sneaker called the RKK Air Force 1 Ultra Flyknit.

name: Sherry Brydson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Sherry Brydson is one of six billionaire heirs to the media and publishing empire founded by her grandfather Roy Thomson (d. 1976).
The family's biggest holding: more than 310 million shares of Thomson Reuters.
Thomson owns around 23% of the business, the largest stake of any of the heirs, through the family's investment firm, Woodbridge.
The family's other assets include the Toronto-based Globe and Mail newspaper, and the Montreal Canadiens and Winnipeg Jets sports teams.

name: Zhang Hejun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Zhang Hejun is the chairman of Ningbo Deye Technology, a supplier of products ranging from energy storage systems and inverters to dehumidifiers and solar air conditioners.
Zhang founded Deye in the eastern Chinese city of Ningbo in 1990. It went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2021 and has over 6,000 employees today.
Deye's business partners include Midea, Haier, TCL and AUX.
Zhang's son Dongye serves as company vice chairman and CEO; older son Dongbin is a director.

name: Lin Li
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2007-2026)
forbes_bio: Lin Li is the chairman of investment firm Liye Group, which has interests in sectors such as healthcare, metals and green energy.
The group is a shareholder of ChinaLin Securities and Tencent-backed online bank WeBank.
Lin's son, Lin Dibang, is the chairman of Shenzhen-based drug maker Cali Biosciences. It planned for an IPO in Hong Kong which didn't go through.
The elder Lin worked at several local branches of the Bank of China before founding Liye in 1995.

name: Ling Tang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Ling Tang is a pre-IPO investor in AI-powered advertising technology company AppLovin, which went public on the Nasdaq in 2021.
Tang owns 5% of AppLovin through an entity called Angel Pride Holdings Ltd.
Tang is one of eight billionaires from AppLovin, including the company's cofounder and CEO Adam Foroughi.
Little is known about Ling Tang, though securities filings list a business address for her on the same street in Hong Kong as another mysterious billionaire AppLovin investor, Hao Tang.

name: Zhou Chaonan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Hurun China (2023-2026); Hurun Self-Made Women (2023-2025)
forbes_bio: Zhou Chaonan is the chairman of Range Intelligent Computing Technology Group, a provider of data center services.
Zhou worked as a teacher briefly before finding a job at a state-owned logistics hub in her home town of Hengyang in Hunan Province.
She then worked for various state-owned firms for almost two decades, and didn't launch her own business until 2000 -- when Zhou was already in her 40s.
Zhou officially set up Range in 2009. The company went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in a backdoor listing in 2022.
forbes_facts: Her given name literally means better than man in Chinese. Zhou's father hoped she could live up to Chairman Mao's famous quote: Women hold up half the sky.

name: Katharina von Baumbach
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Katharina von Baumbach is an heir to the Boehringer Ingelheim fortune, a company best known as the largest private player in the pharmaceutical industry.
Founded in 1885, the company grew by making ingredients for pharmacies, textile merchants and the food industry; and boasted a workforce of 1,500 by 1939.
Today, Boehringer Ingelheim, whose most well-known drugs treat COPD, anti-coagulation and type 2 diabetes, employs 53,000 people and has a presence in 130 markets.

name: Scott Kapnick
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Scott Kapnick is founder and CEO of HPS Investment Partners, one of the world's biggest alternative credit managers with $149 billion in assets.
He spent 21 years at Goldman Sachs, rising to become co-head of investment banking and co-CEO of Goldman Sachs International.
He left Goldman in 2007 to join hedge fund Highbridge Capital after its sale to JPMorgan, eventually building up its credit arm HPS.
Kapnick was CEO of Highbridge from 2013 until 2016, when he and the principals bought HPS from JPMorgan in a carveout. Assets have since swelled.
He sold HPS to BlackRock in July 2025 for around $12 billion in BlackRock stock.
forbes_facts: His father was Arthur Andersen CEO Harvey Kapnick, who left the now defunct accounting firm in 1979 after raising concerns over conflicts of interest.

name: Wendy Abrams
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Wendy Abrams is a shareholder of Illinois-based medical supplies giant Medline, which her father Jon Mills and uncle Jim Mills founded in 1966.

The extended Mills family, which includes four other billionaires, owns roughly 18% of the company, which IPO'd on the Nasdaq in December 2025 and ended its first trading day with a market cap of more than $55 billion.
The Mills family previously sold 79% of Medline to a group of private equity firms in a leveraged buyout that valued the company at more than $30 billion in 2021.

Abrams' cousin Charlie Mills served as Medline's CEO for 26 years until 2023, while her brother Andy Mills served as president during that same period. Charlie still serves as chairman and Andy still sits on the board.
Abrams' husband Jim Abrams served as chief operating officer of Medline from 1997 to 2023. The company is now run by non-family executives.

name: Amos Hostetter Jr
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Amos Hostetter Jr. made a fortune in the 1990s as cable TV pioneer and now is most active in philanthropy.
He set out with an MBA and $1,500 in the 1960s to invest in a cable TV company that eventually became Continental Cablevision.
He sold it to US West for $11 billion in 1996.
His family's Barr Foundation has donated more than $1.7 billion to support the arts and education and to fight climate change.
Hostetter also runs Pilot House Ventures, an early-stage investment firm.
forbes_facts: Hostetter owns seaside property on Nantucket.
The Barr Foundation, with $2.5 billion in assets, has donated more than $1.5 billion since 1999.
